Subject: Autumn trail notes from the Northbay crew
CTA: Read the autumn trail prep guide -> https://www.northbaysupply.com/guides/autumn-trail-prep
Body: Hey,

Fall hiking has its own rhythm. The crowds thin out, the light goes golden by 4 p.m., and the temperature swings between trailhead and summit can catch you off guard if you haven't updated your kit since summer.

A few practical notes heading into the season:

**Layer for the swing, not just the summit.**
Morning starts in the 40s °F can turn into midday 60s on south-facing ridges, then drop fast again once you lose the sun. Plan your layers so you can add and shed without stopping for more than a minute.

**Mud and wet leaves are serious traction hazards.**
Wet hardwood leaf litter on a descent behaves a lot like wet rock. Slow your pace earlier than feels necessary on the way down.

**Daylight is the resource that runs out fastest.**
Sunset is moving up roughly a minute earlier every day right now. Build a turnaround time into your plan and stick to it — a headlamp is backup, not a strategy.

**Check your rain layer before you need it.**
If your shell has been sitting in a gear bag since spring, take it out, check the seams, and do a quick DWR refresh if water is no longer beading on the fabric.

**Pack a insulating layer even on 'warm' days.**
A stopped hiker cools down faster than most people expect. An extra mid-layer weighs little and matters a lot if someone in your group tweaks an ankle and has to wait.

We'll be sharing gear picks built around these conditions in the coming weeks. In the meantime, we've put together a full autumn trail prep guide on the site — conditions by region, a layer-weight reference, and a short checklist you can print before your next trip.

Get out there while the color holds.

— The Northbay Supply team
